one_liner: C++20 SIMD DSP framework whose any-length FFT tracks or beats FFTW in vendor and LIGO/KAGRA benchmarks; GPL or paid license.
what_it_does: KFR is a DSP framework (filters, resampling, convolution, audio I/O, tensors, SIMD math) whose DFT module provides complex, real, multidimensional and DCT-II/III transforms of any positive length in float or double. The main API is a reusable dft_plan<T> / dft_plan_real<T> / dft_plan_md<T,D> with execute(out, in, temp, inverse) and a caller-sized scratch buffer; KFR 7.1 added ngfft, a non-owning power-of-two API with caller-supplied twiddles and no scratch. A C API exposes a subset (FFT and filters). It is not FFTW-API compatible.
how_it_is_fast: Transforms run on KFR's own vec<T,N> SIMD layer (SSE2 to AVX-512, NEON, RVV) rather than relying on auto-vectorization, with multiarchitecture builds dispatching to the best kernel at runtime on x86. Power-of-two sizes use a four-step (DIF half plus DIT half, the 'sandwich') decomposition whose split is chosen from hard-coded per-architecture tables that switch layout once the data exceeds 32 KiB (AVX) or 128 KiB (Apple NEON). Other sizes use mixed-radix stages with fixed SIMD butterflies for radices 2-10 plus a generic butterfly, and Bluestein's algorithm where needed. There is no runtime measurement or wisdom phase, so plan creation is deterministic.
when_to_use: Repeated fixed-size 1D FFTs (power-of-two or arbitrary, including primes) in float or double where FFTW's GPL is acceptable but its planning time or wisdom management is not
Audio and real-time DSP pipelines that also need FIR/IIR filters, FFT convolution, sample-rate conversion and audio file I/O from one library
Cross-platform builds (x86 SSE2-AVX-512, ARM/AArch64 NEON, RISC-V RVV, WebAssembly, iOS/Android) that want one FFT code base with runtime CPU dispatch on x86
Real-time callbacks with a fixed power-of-two size: ngfft has no allocation and no scratch at execution time
Projects that can pay for KFR's commercial license and want an FFT outside FFTW's licensing
when_not_to_use: Closed-source or permissively licensed products that will not buy a commercial license: KFR is GPLv2+ otherwise

MSVC-only toolchains: the DFT module is off by default with MSVC, the docs warn of lower DFT performance, and a Release-mode MSVC build produced a wrong 2^19 real FFT (issue #272, labeled compiler bug)
Multithreaded single large transforms: no internal threading is documented, and its own benchmark harness disables multithreading
Strided, transposed or non-contiguous multidimensional data: MD plans require contiguous row-major tensors, and real MD transforms require an even last axis
When you need proof that it beats a tuned FFTW (FFTW_MEASURE/PATIENT) on your CPU: the published comparisons use FFTW_ESTIMATE or do not state planner flags

integration.form: static lib (DFT, DSP, IO and audio modules are compiled libraries via CMake; the SIMD/expression core is header-only); optional C API library
integration.dependencies: none beyond a C++20 standard library; CMake 3.16+ to build
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; Clang 16+, GCC 11+, MSVC 2022 (19.30+), Xcode 13+; Clang recommended for best performance
integration.platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, WebAssembly; x86/x86-64 (SSE2-AVX-512), ARM/AArch64 (NEON), RISC-V 64 with RVV (VLEN >= 128, Linux, Clang); runtime dispatch only on x86
integration.thread_safety: An initialized dft_plan or ngfft plan is read-only during execute and can be shared across threads if each call has its own data and scratch buffer; the dft_cache used by dft()/realdft() is mutex-protected

gotchas: No transform is normalized: forward then inverse returns N times the input (2/N for the DCT pair)
Real-spectrum layout depends on dft_pack_format (CCs default vs Perm); ngfft real transforms always use Perm, and irealdft infers an even length from the buffer size
Building the DFT module is memory-heavy (vcpkg CI out-of-memory in issue #261); KFR_CLASSIC_FFT restores the pre-7.1 FFT path
ngfft twiddle buffers must be cache-line aligned and outlive the plan; ngfft_twiddle_count returns SIZE_MAX for sizes unsupported on the active architecture
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick KFR over PocketFFT, PFFFT or muFFT when you want SIMD speed on arbitrary 1D lengths plus a full DSP toolkit and can accept GPL or a paid license; over FFTS because FFTS is unmaintained. Pick VectorFFT only for x86 double c2c work that wants an MIT license and an MKL-beating claim, and VkFFT for GPUs.
verified_claims_summary: The independent evidence is an LVK (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA) proceedings paper (arXiv 2503.14292, Fig. 6): complex forward in-place FFTs on a local Osaka cluster show KFR 6.0.2 with higher MFlops than FFTW 3.3.10 (Clang), shown only as graphs, with no CPU model or planner flags and using a harness first written by KFR's author. KFR's own README graphs (KFR 3.0.5-rc, clang 7.0.1, AVX2, Windows) show roughly 1.3-3x FFTW 3.3.8 on powers of two, but its kfrlib/fft-benchmark harness plans FFTW with FFTW_ESTIMATE, which understates FFTW.
status_note: Actively maintained (KFR 7.1.0 released 2026-08-18, about 1.9k stars, 18 open issues); usable as GPLv2+ code or under a paid commercial license, with prebuilt release packages and CMake integration.
